clue.text: Childhood as imagined?

parts.note: the phrase for something existing only in one's imagination, split as two words, also names the earliest years of life

explanation.surface: A wistful question about whether our memories of being young are only invented.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is 'in fancy', meaning only in the imagination; read as one, it is the first stage of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest period of a person's life, babyhood, is a synonym for childhood.

clue.text: One's beginning to seethe over European Union matter

parts.note: one's read as 'one is', the Roman numeral I plus the verb, gives IS

indicators.note: the beginning of the word seethe gives its first letter only
in a down clue, over means the letters for European Union are turned upwards, read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone starts to fume about some business involving Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns EU into UE, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter under discussion is an issue, a topic or question at hand.

clue.text: Basic measure to finance a section of asylum?

parts.note: to fund something is to finance it
a ward of an old asylum could be called a mental unit

explanation.surface: Suggests paying for a single ward in a psychiatric hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A base unit in physics, like the metre or second, is the fundamental standard of measurement.

clue.text: Close attention needed after negligent start

indicators.note: the piece for attention comes after the letter from negligent
the start of the word negligent is its first letter

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Careful focus is required after a careless beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Close as an adjective, nearby or not far, is a synonym.

clue.text: The old country's railway guards

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of the, so the old version of 'the'
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: Sounds like the security staff of an old nation's train network.
explanation.walkthrough: The yeomanry were volunteer cavalry units in Britain, formed to guard the home country.
explanation.definitionFit: Volunteer mounted troops raised for home defence acted as guards of the realm.

clue.text: Gave Satisfaction in exchange for Slade EP

indicators.note: letters given in exchange are swapped around and traded into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A record swap: someone handed over a Slade record and got (the Rolling Stones') Satisfaction back.
explanation.walkthrough: Slade were a 1970s British glam rock band, an EP is a short record, and Satisfaction is a famous Rolling Stones song: the capital S hides the plain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to give them satisfaction, so the past tense fits.

clue.text: Former policeman identified stripper

definitions.meaning: an old slang name for a police officer, after Sir Robert Peel who founded the force
something or someone that peels, such as a tool removing skin or paint

explanation.surface: An ex-cop is unmasked as a striptease artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel's officers were nicknamed after him, and a tool or person that removes outer layers is one that peels.

clue.text: Final one to enter English town showing flexibility

indicators.note: the pieces for final and one go inside, entering between the others

parts.note: a city is a large town
last means final
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is the last to arrive in a town in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final one' looks like a single idea but gives two pieces; 'to enter' places them inside the town with its English prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: Elasticity is the capacity to stretch and bend, a synonym of flexibility.

clue.text: Celebrating mass with oily unction … thus?

definitions.text: Celebrating mass with oily unction … thus?

indicators.note: celebrating suggests a festive jumbling, so these letters are mixed up anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest saying Mass with greasy, unctuous piety: is that how it is done?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: an oily, pious priest at Mass would behave in a smugly holy way.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with smug, affected piety is what a greasily devout celebrant would display.

clue.text: Study of ingested matter that is included in newfangled CID test

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes inside the rearranged letters
newfangled means novel, so the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A new forensic test by the police detectives (CID) looks at what was swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, so the police surface hides plain fodder; 'newfangled' gives DTETICS and 'included in' slots the Latin abbreviation in after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietetics is the science of nutrition, the study of food the body takes in.

clue.text: Perform comic opera in foreign location

parts.note: to sing is to perform music

indicators.note: comic suggests something played for laughs, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer is asked to stage a comic opera abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Singapore is an Asian city-state, a place abroad from the setter's British viewpoint.

clue.text: Schwarzenegger cut crusts off sandwiches

indicators.note: trimming the crusts removes the outer edge, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: sarnies is British slang for sandwiches

explanation.surface: Arnold Schwarzenegger trims the crusts from his sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: SARNIES (British slang for sandwiches) loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The familiar nickname of actor Arnold Schwarzenegger.

clue.text: Indication of mistake along with a mark added to English test

parts.note: a cross marks a wrong answer
M is the abbreviation for the German mark, an old currency

explanation.surface: A teacher's cross and a grade are written on an English paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An examination is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Non-washable clothes can be stitched up so

definitions.meaning: garments that cannot go in the machine are carried to a dry-cleaning shop
stitched up is slang for cheated or swindled

explanation.surface: Clothes that cannot be washed may as well be sewn together.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is idiom for being fleeced, and literally where delicate garments are sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fleeced or swindled is the idiom; literally, clothes needing dry cleaning are carried to a shop for it.

clue.text: Albert, Ken and I disciplined Victoria's kid

indicators.note: disciplined suggests being knocked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Three people take a firm hand with Queen Victoria's child.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria here is the Australian state, not the queen, and Australians call a small child an ankle-biter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankle-biter is Australian slang for a toddler, so a child in Victoria.

clue.text: See 12
Hardly a radiant smile from this supporter

parts.note: someone cross, angry, is hardly radiant
a beam is a broad smile

explanation.surface: An angry face hardly beams, so this one is no fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly a radiant smile' reads as one phrase but splits: an angry person, then a grin.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal timber that holds up a structure is a support.

clue.text: Seafood some chefs adeptly make for starters — very good

indicators.note: the starters of the words are their first letters

parts.note: PI, short for pious, means very good in crossword usage

explanation.surface: A recipe line: skilled cooks make this as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustine tails, a seafood dish.

clue.text: Leaving about end of day, celebrating

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a parting is a leaving or departure

indicators.note: the end of the word day is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone heads off around dusk, in festive mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Partying is having a celebration.

clue.text: Better by air

parts.note: better as a verb, meaning to beat, done in the air: to surpass in flight

explanation.surface: A claim that flying is the superior way to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass another in flight is the sense of this verb.

clue.text: Rather old but no longer on the shelf?

definitions.meaning: said of goods too old to be sold

explanation.surface: An older person, at least, is no longer single and unwanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the shelf' usually means unmarried; here it is a shop shelf, where expired stock is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being too old covers a person getting on and food expired and taken off sale.

clue.text: Takes little part in troubles

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: ados are fusses or troubles
PT is the abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: Someone plays a small role in a time of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PT inside ADOS; 'little' signals the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt is to take on as one's own, as a child or an idea.

clue.text: See 18
The person in charge is a stud

definitions.meaning: a raised knob, as on a shield or ornament

explanation.surface: The manager is a ladies' man.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a chief, and also a round raised ornament on a surface, like a stud.

clue.text: Rest, finding shelter in special environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the letters for special enclose the other piece

parts.note: a lee is a sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: Resting by taking cover in a protected habitat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' is the container signal: the abbreviation for special wraps round the sheltered side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep is rest for the body, as a noun or verb.

clue.text: Good kid, happy

parts.note: a lad is a boy, a kid

explanation.surface: A well-behaved child is cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad means pleased or happy.

clue.text: He painted in modern style

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: An artist who worked in a contemporary manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German surrealist painter.

clue.text: Old man suffering on rough seas needed somewhere to sleep

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
ill means unwell, suffering

indicators.note: rough seas are churned up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seasick old sailor needs a bunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A paillasse is a straw mattress, a bed.

clue.text: Story told of Egyptian god becoming Persian one

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word for story is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a myth is a story
Ra is the Egyptian sun god; 'of' him gives Ra's, the possessive

explanation.surface: A legend of an Egyptian deity becomes that of a Persian one.
explanation.walkthrough: MYTH said out loud gives MITH; Ra's makes RAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mithras was a god of Persian origin, worshipped also in the Roman mystery cults.

clue.text: Dizzy, riding faster!

parts.note: giddy means dizzy
a jockey up is riding, mounted on a horse

explanation.surface: A light-headed rider urges the horse on.
explanation.definitionFit: The command to a horse to go quicker is a call for more speed.
